question: Why is my mobile internet so slow?
answer:
Slow mobile internet is usually caused by:
*   Network congestion in your area
*   Being in a low-signal zone
*   Reaching your high-speed data cap (which throttles speed to 512 kbps)

**Try this:**
1.  Toggle airplane mode off and on to force a network reconnect.

If the issue persists, please call 611 or use the MyTelecom app for further assistance.

sources.content:
Question: Why is my mobile internet so slow?
Answer: Slow speeds are usually caused by network congestion in your area, being in a low-signal zone, or reaching your high-speed data cap. Try toggling airplane mode off and on to force a network reconnect. If your high-speed data is exhausted your speed is throttled to 512 kbps.

Question: What should I do if I have no signal at home?
Answer: First check our coverage map at telecom.example.com/coverage. If coverage is shown as good in your area try restarting your phone and reseating the SIM card. Persistent issues may require a network investigation - call 611.

Question: How do I activate 4G/LTE on my phone?
Answer: Go to Settings > Mobile Network > Preferred Network Type and select 4G/LTE. Make sure your SIM supports 4G and your plan includes it. If the option is missing, contact support to check your account.

Issue: Extremely slow 4G speeds (below 1 Mbps)
Description: Customer's speed test consistently shows 0.3–0.8 Mbps download on 4G in a city centre location.
Resolution: Identified the local cell as congested during peak hours (5–8 pm). Enabled carrier aggregation on the customer's profile to utilise a secondary band. Speeds improved to 12–18 Mbps in follow-up test.

Issue: No internet access
Description: Customer reports complete loss of mobile internet after switching from 3G to 4G mode.
Resolution: Guided customer to toggle airplane mode and reset APN settings. Internet restored after APN was reset to default (internet.telecom.example).

Issue: Number port taking too long
Description: Customer submitted a port-in request 6 hours ago and the number is still active on the old provider.
Resolution: Old provider had placed an admin hold on the number due to an outstanding balance. Advised customer to settle the balance with the old provider. Port completed within 1 hour of balance clearance.

question: I see a charge on my bill I don't recognize, what is it?
answer:
To identify the unrecognized charge, please follow these steps:

1.  Log in to the **MyTelecom app**.
2.  Go to **Billing** > **Itemised Bill**.
3.  Review the list, which shows every call, SMS, and data session with the date, time, and cost.

Common reasons for unexpected charges include:
*   International roaming charges.
*   Premium SMS subscriptions (third-party services).
*   Additional data packs purchased mid-cycle.
*   A plan change.

If you cannot find the charge or need further assistance, please call **611** or use the **MyTelecom app** to contact support.

Question: Why is my bill higher than usual?
Answer: Common reasons for a higher bill: international roaming charges, premium SMS subscriptions, additional data packs purchased mid-cycle, or a plan change. Go to Billing > Itemised Bill in the app to see a full breakdown.

Question: How do I get an itemised bill?
Answer: Log in to MyTelecom > Billing > Download Bill and select PDF. Itemised bills show every call, SMS, and data session with date, time, and cost. Bills are available for the last 12 months.

Question: When is my bill due?
Answer: Your bill is generated on your monthly anniversary date and payment is due 14 days later. You can check your exact due date in the MyTelecom app under Billing > Current Bill.

Issue: Unable to view itemised bill
Description: Customer cannot download the PDF bill — the download button spins indefinitely.
Resolution: Known bug in the web portal affecting accounts with more than 500 itemised events per cycle. Sent the itemised bill manually as a password-protected PDF via email as a workaround. Escalated the portal bug to the engineering team.

Issue: Double charged for monthly plan
Description: Customer's bank statement shows two identical charges of $45 on the same date.
Resolution: Duplicate charge caused by a payment gateway retry during a network timeout. Confirmed only one payment received on our side. Issued a refund of $45 within 3–5 business days and sent confirmation email.

Issue: Unexpected roaming charges
Description: Customer returned from a trip to Spain and received a bill $240 higher than expected. Claims they had a roaming bundle active.
Resolution: Investigated and found the roaming bundle was activated 3 hours after the customer's first data session abroad. Charges prior to bundle activation were billed at standard rates. Offered 50% goodwill credit ($30) on the pre-bundle charges.

question: I hear an echo during phone calls, how do I fix it?
answer:
Based on the provided context, echo issues are typically caused by network configuration settings rather than device faults.

**Action:**
Please contact customer support so an agent can check and reconfigure the echo cancellation settings on the network side.

**How to contact support:**
*   Call **611** (free from your mobile).
*   Use **live chat** in the MyTelecom app (available 8am–10pm).
*   Email **support@telecom.example.com**.

*Note: In a similar case (TK-017), the echo was resolved by remotely reconfiguring the network setting.*

Question: My calls keep dropping. What should I do?
Answer: Call drops are often caused by weak signal, SIM card faults, or a faulty device antenna. Try these steps: 1) Restart the phone 2) Reseat the SIM 3) Test with another SIM if possible 4) Check for network outages via the app.

Question: How do I block unwanted calls and texts?
Answer: You can block a number directly in your phone's call log or contacts app. For persistent spam report the number by texting STOP to 7726. We also offer a free Call Shield service - enable it in MyTelecom > Security.

Question: How do I contact customer support?
Answer: Call 611 (free from your mobile), use live chat in the MyTelecom app available 8am-10pm, email support@telecom.example.com, or visit any of our retail stores. Average call wait time is under 3 minutes.

Issue: Echo on every call
Description: Customer hears their own voice echoed back with a 1-second delay on all outgoing calls.
Resolution: Echo caused by a misconfigured echo cancellation setting on the local RNC. Reconfigured remotely. Customer confirmed echo resolved on a test call.

Issue: Calls going straight to voicemail
Description: All incoming calls reach voicemail immediately even though the phone shows full signal and is not on Do Not Disturb.
Resolution: Call barring had been activated on the account without the customer's knowledge. Deactivated call barring remotely via the HLR. Advised customer to set a new call barring PIN.

Issue: Phone not compatible with VoLTE
Description: Customer's new handset shows voice calls on 3G even though the SIM and plan support VoLTE.
Resolution: Checked the device IMEI against the VoLTE whitelist — handset model was a parallel import not on the approved list. Explained the limitation and offered an upgrade deal. Customer declined and accepted the 3G voice fallback.

2. Troubleshooting Connectivity Issues
Connectivity problems are the most common category of customer complaints. A structured diagnostic approach
resolves the majority of cases without escalation.
Step 1  - Verify signal strength. Open the device's status bar or dial *3001#12345#* (iOS) or use a network signal
app (Android) to view the raw signal level in dBm. A signal above -85 dBm is good; between -85 and -100 dBm is
marginal; below -100 dBm is poor. If signal is weak, moving closer to a window or to a higher floor often helps.

question: How do I check my current data balance?
answer:
You can check your current data balance by doing one of the following:

1.  **Dial *123#** from your mobile phone.
2.  **Log in to the MyTelecom app** and go to **My Usage**. Your remaining balance will be displayed on the dashboard.

sources.content:
Question: How do I check my current data balance?
Answer: Dial *123# from your mobile or log in to the MyTelecom app and go to My Usage. Your remaining data balance will be shown on the dashboard.

Question: How do I check if there is a network outage in my area?
Answer: Open the MyTelecom app > Help > Network Status and enter your postcode. Alternatively check our live status page at telecom.example.com/status. Planned maintenance windows are listed 48 hours in advance.

Question: How do I get an itemised bill?
Answer: Log in to MyTelecom > Billing > Download Bill and select PDF. Itemised bills show every call, SMS, and data session with date, time, and cost. Bills are available for the last 12 months.

Issue: Data balance not updating
Description: Customer purchased a 5 GB add-on pack but the balance still shows the old figure in the app.
Resolution: Billing system had a 30-minute sync delay. Refreshed the customer's session token via backend. Balance updated correctly after cache clear.

Issue: Number port taking too long
Description: Customer submitted a port-in request 6 hours ago and the number is still active on the old provider.
Resolution: Old provider had placed an admin hold on the number due to an outstanding balance. Advised customer to settle the balance with the old provider. Port completed within 1 hour of balance clearance.

Issue: Background apps consuming all mobile data
Description: Customer used 8 GB of data in 3 days and believes their apps are syncing in the background without consent.
Resolution: Reviewed data usage breakdown — a cloud backup app had uploaded 6.2 GB. Educated customer on restricting background data per app in Android settings. Enabled Data Saver mode on the account as a safeguard.

Hotspot (Tethering) Usage: Hotspot usage draws from the same data allowance as device usage. However, some
plans include a separate hotspot sub-allowance. Once the hotspot sub-allowance is exhausted, hotspot speeds
are throttled even if device data remains available. Enterprise and business plans typically have higher or
uncapped hotspot allowances.
Data Usage Monitoring: Customers can monitor real-time usage in the MyTelecom app. Push notifications are

Data Rollover: Some plans include a data rollover feature. Unused high-speed data at the end of a billing cycle is
carried forward to the next cycle, up to a maximum of one month's allowance. Rolled-over data is consumed
before the current cycle's allowance.
Add-On Data Packs: Customers who exhaust their high-speed allowance mid-cycle can purchase add-on data
packs to restore full speeds. Packs activate immediately upon purchase and are valid until the end of the current
billing cycle. Unused add-on data does not roll over.
